stories.headline: Bus driver burnt alive as arson attacks, crude bomb blasts rock Bangladesh
stories.deck: A 60-year-old bus driver was killed in an arson attack on a parked bus in Faridpur. Multiple incidents of vehicle arson and crude bomb explosions were reported across various districts in Bangladesh. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police increased security and arrested 19 individuals linked to these attacks. Investigations are underway to determine those responsible for the violence.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: A 60-year-old bus driver was burnt to death after unidentified miscreants set fire to a parked bus in Bangladesh's Faridpur early Monday, as a series of arson attacks and crude bomb explosions were reported in Dhaka and several other districts.
The deceased, identified as Md Kalachan Sheikh, was sleeping inside a bus belonging to Kishore-Tanay Paribahan near Goalchamat New Bus Stand when it was set on fire, reported Bangladesh Daily New Age (Bangladesh). Firefighters rescued him and took him to Faridpur Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
In another incident, a petrol bomb was hurled at a double-decker bus carrying around 35 students of Islamic University in Jhenaidah on Monday night. The bus, named Diganta, was travelling towards the university campus when the attack took place in the Dragon Bagan area of Shailkupa upazila. No casualties were reported, according to The Daily Star.
In Dhaka, at least two crude bombs exploded in front of Tokyo Square in the Mohammadpur area around 9:15pm on Monday. Police said they were yet to identify those responsible.
Separately, a Basumati Paribahan bus was set on fire in front of the Mirpur-11 Post Office around 9.30pm. 
No one was injured.
In Bogura district, a van carrying jute sacks was set on fire on the Dhaka-Bogura highway in Sherpur upazila on Monday evening. The vehicle was gutted, temporarily disrupting traffic. Firefighters brought the blaze under control.
More buses torched in Dhaka, Savar and Gazipur
The incidents came amid a wider spate of arson attacks and crude bomb explosions across Bangladesh. According to The Daily Star, six buses were set on fire in Savar, Dhaka and Gazipur on Monday.
In Savar, two buses parked along the Dhaka-Aricha highway were torched in the Genda and Baliarpur areas around 1am and 4am, respectively. One was used to transport garment workers, while the other belonged to Itihash Paribahan. The fires damaged the buses' seats and interiors.
In Dhaka, a Lovely Paribahan bus was set on fire beneath the Farmgate metro station in the evening. Another bus, belonging to Basumati Paribahan, was torched under the metro rail line in Mirpur-11 around 9:15pm.
In Gazipur's Kaliakair upazila, two parked buses were set on fire in the Chandra area along the Dhaka-Tangail highway, The Daily Star reported.
Crude bomb explosions were also reported from several parts of Dhaka, including Banasree, Mohakhali, Dhaka University campus and outside the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court.
Police step up security, arrest 19
Amid the attacks, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) set up 160 additional checkpoints at key locations across the capital on Monday and deployed more personnel to prevent further incidents.
DMP Deputy Commissioner (Media) Akhter Hossain told The Daily Star that police had arrested at least 19 people in the preceding 24 hours in connection with recent blasts and attacks. He said many of those arrested were linked to the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned.
Police in Savar also suspected the involvement of the banned Awami League in the two bus arson incidents there. Investigations were under way to identify those responsible.
The attacks come amid heightened political tensions in Bangladesh following the July 2024 uprising that led to the ouster of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina. The Awami League's activities were subsequently banned, and authorities have alleged links of some of its leaders and activists to recent incidents of crude bomb explosions and vehicle arson.

stories.headline: UFC chief Dana White declines Donald Trump's White House job offer
stories.deck: Dana White visited the White House on November 9, and Donald Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room
stories.bodyText:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump's -- apparently jovial -- offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Mr. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday (November 7) that he had asked Mr. White to take on the high-profile post -- but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was "only kidding."
The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday (November 9), and Mr. Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room.
"So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?" Mr. Trump said.
"Thank you for the offer, sir -- for the offer, I have no, no -- I do not want to be in politics," Mr. White replied.
Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody."
The press secretary's post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job.
Mr. Trump's announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to "violent Fighter and Warrior" Mr. White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party's stunning midterm elections defeat.
Mr. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year.
But there was also some scepticism about the president's announcement, and Mr. Trump said Sunday (November 8) night that he had been joking.
‘Beat the hell out of you’
Leading out Mr. White to the podium on Monday (November 9), Mr. Trump said he had been "having a little fun."
"He's a great guy," Mr. Trump told the room full of reporters. "The only problem is he'll talk for a little while and then he's going to beat the hell out of you."
Standing at the lectern and wearing a black t-shirt and jacket, Mr. White looked like he might be more comfortable in the octagon -- the ring used for UFC fights.
"I've always wanted to do this. Who has the first question?" he joked -- before quickliy adding: "I have zero political aspirations."
Mr. White added that "the last 24 hours of my life has been insane" since Mr. Trump made the announcement.
Asked by a journalist to confirm he had said no to the job, Mr. White added: "I don't tell the president 'no' to anything... I didn't want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first."
Mr. Trump then took a series of questions on more weighty matters, from the Iran and Ukraine wars to the possible impeachment of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and a spy scandal engulfing Nvidia boss Jensen Huang.

stories.headline: China hits $1 trillion trade surplus milestone for second year in a row
stories.deck: China's trade surplus surpassed $1 trillion in the first ten months, driven primarily by high-tech product demand. Exports increased significantly due to the global AI investment boom, although imports also grew faster than expected. Domestic consumption remains weak, which has pressured manufacturers to seek overseas markets for growth. Trade tensions with the European Union and the United…
stories.bodyText:
China's trade surplus crossed $1 trillion in the first 10 months of the year, as strong global demand for high-tech products, fuelled by the race to build artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, helped offset weak domestic consumption.
The surplus reached $1.04 trillion between January and October, according to customs data released on Tuesday.
China has now recorded a trade surplus of more than $1 trillion for a second consecutive year, reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025.
Exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier in US dollar terms, slightly below September's 36.3% increase but higher than the 33.5% growth forecast by economists in a Reuters poll.
Imports grew 41.6%, accelerating from 31% in September and beating the poll's median forecast of 32%.
Despite the stronger import growth, China's trade surplus narrowed to $105.3 billion in October from $133.5 billion in September.
The export performance reflects China's growing reliance on overseas demand as subdued domestic consumption and a prolonged property market downturn weigh on its economy.
The global AI investment boom has supported sales of Chinese technology products, including semiconductors and electronics, but the expanding surplus is also raising concerns among trading partners.
AI demand supports exports, but trade tensions persist
Much of China's export growth this year has been driven by the global push to expand AI infrastructure. Analysts expect demand for Chinese technology products to remain strong into 2027, although the outlook will depend on how long the investment boom lasts.
“The outlook for exports depends on how long the AI boom will last,” Macquarie analysts wrote, adding that exports could accelerate further in the fourth quarter before beginning to slow from the first quarter of 2027.
Dave Chia, an economist at Moody's Analytics, also expects Chinese exports to remain strong through the rest of the year, led by electronics and automobiles.
However, the expanding surplus could intensify trade tensions, particularly with the European Union.
European leaders have called for further trade restrictions on China after reaching an agreement with Beijing to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle exports to the bloc over the next few years.
Since the measures have yet to take effect, manufacturers are expected to bring forward shipments, supporting exports in the near term.
“The risk of additional tariffs and other trade barriers will remain elevated in 2027, particularly as Chinese manufacturers continue expanding their presence in overseas markets,” said Joe Peissel, lead macroeconomist at Trivium China.
The US-China trade relationship also remains uncertain. Beijing on Monday officially announced a two-month extension of its trade truce with Washington, which was due to expire on November 10.
However, China said last week that any expansion of its purchases of US agricultural goods would depend on the implementation of the agreed reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement.
China's trade surplus with the US narrowed slightly to $32.71 billion in October from $34.01 billion in September, but the gap remains a point of friction between the two economies.
Trade is expected to feature prominently in the planned meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen later this month.
The two leaders are expected to meet for the third time this year.
Weak domestic demand adds to export dependence
The strong export performance comes against the backdrop of subdued consumer spending in China. A prolonged downturn in the property market has weakened household wealth and confidence, leaving domestic demand under pressure.
The weakness has also pushed Chinese manufacturers to look overseas for customers. Automobile exports maintained a solid pace of growth in October, while domestic vehicle sales recorded their 12th consecutive monthly decline, according to separate industry data.
AP cited analysts who said overcapacity in several industries, excess domestic savings and weak domestic demand were pushing Chinese companies to sell more goods abroad. Alicia García-Herrero, chief economist for Asia Pacific at Natixis, said the situation was not sustainable.
Businesses are also facing intense competition at home. Cinders Zhou, who sells eyewear for a manufacturer in the eastern Chinese city of Linhai, told AP that competition had increasingly centred on price as products across the industry became more similar.
“It comes down to product quality, or rather the increasingly the lack of it across the industry, since there's significant homogenization,” Zhou said. “That has forced everyone to compete on price.”
Greater dependence on overseas markets also leaves China's economy more exposed to a slowdown in global demand or further trade restrictions. Analysts have warned that any correction in the AI industry could hurt exports of chips and electronics.
“If the AI boom slows or turns into a correction, lower chip and electronics prices and smaller shipping volumes would hit China's exports hard,” Chia said, according to AP.
Oil imports fall despite supply concerns
China's oil imports fell 13.3% in October compared with a year earlier, although shipments reached their highest level since March as buyers sought supplies following disruptions to Middle East flows caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The trade figures come ahead of the APEC summit, where trade policy and tariffs are expected to be among the key issues in discussions between Trump and Xi. The two sides had previously proposed a $60 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts following their September summit in Washington, including around $17 billion worth of US agricultural goods.
While Chinese officials have maintained that Beijing is not seeking to expand its trade surplus and wants more balanced global trade, the latest figures underline the importance of overseas demand to the country's export-led growth.

stories.headline: Renowned Malayalam cinematographer Shaji Kumar dies at 57
stories.bodyText: Kochi: Renowned Malayalam cinematographer Shaji Kumar, whose works include the blockbuster Mohanlal-starrers Pulimurugan, Naran and Thudarum, died at the age of 57, film industry sources said here on Tuesday. . Kumar was in Alappuzha for the shooting of an upcoming film starring Dileep when he experienced physical discomfort at his hotel room on Saturday night. . He informed the film’s director, Ullas Krishna, about his discomfort and was initially taken to a nearby hospital. He was later shifted to a private hospital here. . Though his condition improved after admission and he was able to speak normally, his health deteriorated again on Sunday night, sources said. .Actor Prakash Raj criticises UDF government in Keralam over suspension of students at Sanskrit University. His unexpected death has left members of the Malayalam film industry shocked and saddened. . The FEFKA Directors' Union condoled his death, paying tribute to the cinematographer for his contributions to Malayalam cinema. . A disciple of veteran cinematographer Vipin Mohan, Kumar began his career working on several films before establishing himself as an independent cinematographer. . Over the years, he became one of the familiar names behind the visuals of several successful Malayalam films. . Starting his career in the era of film cameras, he was known for his skill in lighting, colour composition and framing. . He successfully adapted to digital filmmaking, keeping pace with changing technology and new styles of visual storytelling. . He worked with several leading directors, including Joshiy, Shaji Kailas, V M Vinu, M Padmakumar and Vaishakh. . He also collaborated with younger filmmakers, including Tharun Moorthy. . His recent cinematography assignments included Athimanoharam, starring Mohanlal and directed by Tharun Moorthy, and Suresh Gopi’s Ottakomban. . Hailing from Thiruvananthapuram, Kumar had been living in Perumbavoor for several years. . He is survived by his wife, Smitha, and sons Aryan and Sooryan. . His filmography includes Naran, Pulimurugan, Ramaleela, Odiyan, Madhura Raja, Ittymaani: Made in China, Night Drive, Pathonpatham Noottandu, Bandra, Once Upon a Time in Kochi and Thudarum.

stories.headline: Demonetisation helped reduce terrorism, end Naxalism: Odisha BJP
stories.bodyText: Bhubaneswar: Odisha BJP on Monday claimed that the demonetisation exercise carried out by Prime Minister Narendra Modi 10 years ago needed to be duly recognised, as it paved the way to end terrorism and Naxalism and also boost the economy. . The claims were made by state BJP spokesperson Satyabrata Panda at a press conference on the occasion of the 10th anniversary of the demonetisation exercise. .Demonetisation @ 10 | What did India gain?. The Union government on November 8, 2016, announced the demonetisation of all Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 Mahatma Gandhi Series banknotes. . “The bold decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on demonetisation has not only disrupted the flow of cash to extremists but also neutralised the old counterfeit. Demonetisation played a significant role in invalidating currency notes and bringing financial transactions into the formal banking and digital systems," Panda said. . "In the past, Naxalites dared to abduct district collectors and MLAs in Odisha; however, that situation no longer exists. Demonetisation has made a major contribution toward this change,” he told reporters here. . Stating that unaccounted cash, counterfeit notes, and ‘hawala’ transactions were fuelling corruption and violence, the BJP leader asserted that demonetisation dealt a decisive blow to this entire ecosystem. . He said the contribution of demonetisation in subsequent security operations, developmental initiatives, and economic reforms deserves to be duly recognised and evaluated. . Panda said that demonetisation immediately rendered the high-value counterfeit currency notes, specifically the old Rs 500 and Rs 1000 denominations printed in Pakistan, worthless. . “Following demonetisation, approximately Rs 97.75 lakh was seized from various Maoist groups. In Odisha, significant amounts of now-invalid currency, which had been buried underground by the Maoists, were discovered. This move to disrupt the funding of extremists was part of a comprehensive anti-Maoist campaign,” he said. . He pointed out that when the number of incidents of Naxal violence across the country stood at 1,936 in 2010, no district remains on the list of Maoist-affected areas now. . This is a collective success, stemming from security operations, intelligence coordination, the development of roads and connectivity, rehabilitation, and poverty alleviation, alongside demonetization, Panda claimed. . “In Jammu and Kashmir, the number of attacks and violent incidents perpetrated by terrorists has also dropped from 228 in 2018 to 12 in 2025. Due to the BJP government's comprehensive counter-terrorism policy, such incidents have declined by 95 per cent. Cutting off terror financing is a crucial component of this policy," the BJP leader said. . He added that according to Reserve Bank figures, the number of counterfeit notes detected within the banking system declined from 7,62,072 in 2016–17 to 2,29,746 in 2025–26, a reduction of approximately 70 per cent. .From demonetisation to Vande Mataram: The politics of keeping India on edge. He said positive changes were also observed in the tax sector. . In 2017–18, net direct tax collections increased by 18 per cent, and the number of income tax returns filed rose by 25 per cent. . The number of new tax filers grew from 85.51 lakh in the previous year to approximately 1.07 crore. Between November 2016 and March 2017, Rs 900 crore was seized during income tax raids, and approximately Rs 7,961 crore of undisclosed income was declared, Panda said. . Demonetisation and the subsequent scrutiny of bank deposit data contributed to better tax compliance. . A study by the Reserve Bank estimated that unusual cash deposits amounting to Rs 1.6 to 1.7 lakh crore were made into certain types of bank accounts. This data provided an opportunity for further investigation, he said.

briefs.headline: Russia-US diesel deal delivers results? Lavrov claims prices have already fallen
briefs.deck: Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov stated that an agreement allows Russia to resume diesel exports to the US. The arrangement aims to stabilize energy markets and improve energy security amid rising fuel prices. Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy infrastructure continue, impacting fuel shortages in several regions of Russia. Despite concerns over regulatory issues, the US Treasury Department…
briefs.bodyText:
Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov has said an agreement allowing Russia to resume diesel exports to the United States and global markets is already being implemented and has helped bring prices down.
In an article published in Moscow daily Kommersant on Tuesday, Lavrov said the arrangement was an important contribution to energy security. He also argued that Russia did not use its economy to score political points against countries it considered adversaries or competitors.
“Since 2022, we have supplied Europe with energy resources worth $320 billion,” Lavrov wrote.
“An important contribution to energy security was the agreement between the Russian and US leaders to suspend restrictions on the export of Russian diesel. We have already started implementing it, which immediately brought prices down.”
US President Donald Trump announced the deal on October 9. Under the arrangement, Russia agreed to make 300,000 metric tonnes, or 2.25 million barrels, of diesel available immediately to the US and global markets, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and a further 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.
The Trump administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel to facilitate the exports.
The move came as the US president sought to bring down fuel prices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which his Republican Party lost.
US-bound shipments face uncertainty
Lavrov did not provide figures to support his claim that the agreement had lowered diesel prices.
US diesel futures have fallen about 11% since the deal was announced, according to Reuters.
However, diesel prices at US pumps were at a record high last week when Americans voted, according to price tracker GasBuddy.
The arrangement has also faced uncertainty over whether Russian fuel would reach the US.
Two sanctioned tankers that had initially declared destinations on the US East Coast changed course, while a third vessel travelling across the North Atlantic changed its destination from New York to “for orders”, according to news agency AP.
The report said the proposed imports had yet to result in a confirmed US delivery. Analysts also questioned whether the shipments would reach American ports, citing regulatory and sanctions-related concerns.
New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill had advised port and terminal operators in the state to reject Russian fuel shipments, warning of possible legal consequences. A bipartisan group of US senators also urged Trump to abandon the arrangement, arguing that it could provide financial support to Moscow.
The US Treasury Department, however, maintained that its temporary authorisation for Russian diesel transactions was consistent with previous actions and “in compliance with all applicable laws”.
The exemption was issued for the sale, delivery, unloading and import of Russian diesel until April 7.
Separately, Russian deputy foreign minister Alexander Pankin said on Monday that the diesel arrangement could provide an opportunity for the gradual restoration of business and other ties between Moscow and Washington.
He told the TASS state news agency that the deal could “serve as a foundation for the gradual restoration of business and other ties between our countries”.
Lavrov raises Ukraine strikes on Russian energy infrastructure
In his Kommersant article, Lavrov said Russia was working to stabilise global energy markets and ensure energy security, as well as the balanced and sustainable development of countries and regions.
He also accused Ukraine of ignoring Trump's calls to stop attacks on Russian energy infrastructure.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last week that Kyiv's forces were continuing their strikes.
Russian media have reported that fuel shortages have returned in at least half a dozen Russian regions following Ukrainian attacks on at least eight major oil refineries over the past two weeks.

briefs.headline: Property inherited by son after partition is individual, not ancestral: SC
briefs.bodyText: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has ruled that property inherited by a son from his father following a partition of the grandfather’s estate is held by the son in his individual capacity. A grandson does not acquire any right by birth in such property under Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956. A bench of Justices Augustine George Masih and Sunita Agarwal dismissed an appeal filed by a minor through his mother, holding that the property in question had lost its coparcenary character after partition and could not be claimed as joint family property. The court observed that under the codified Hindu law, the Schedule to Section 8 lists Class I heirs as including the son but not the son’s son while the living father is alive. It specifically includes the son of a predeceased son. .Legal heir under Hindu Succession Act must be party to partition suit; compromise decree without them nullity: SC. “To say that when a son inherits the property in the situation contemplated by Section 8 he takes it as Karta of his own undivided family would be impossible,” the bench said. The express words of Section 8 must prevail and cannot be ignored, the court emphasised. In November 06, 2026 judgement, Justice Agrawal for the bench noted that the right of a son’s son in his grandfather’s property during the lifetime of his father, which existed under the pre-1956 personal Hindu law, was not expressly saved by the legislature when the Hindu Succession Act was enacted. In the present case, the appellant had sought partition and possession of a half share in a property measuring 1,811 sq ft in Chennai. He claimed it was joint family property belonging to his grandfather, late N Ramakrishnan, which had been inherited by him along with his father. The father had sold the property through two sale deeds in 1997 to third parties after receiving it under a compromise decree in a 1993 partition suit filed by his sister. The trial court had granted a preliminary decree of partition. The first appellate court and the Madras High Court set it aside, holding that the father had become the absolute owner of the share allotted to him. The Supreme Court upheld this view. .Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on plea challenging gender bias in Muslim inheritance laws. It pointed out that upon the death of N Ramakrishnan, succession opened under Section 8. The Class I heirs succeeded as tenants-in-common and not as joint tenants. Under the 1994 compromise decree, each heir became the exclusive owner of the property falling to his or her share. With the partition, the property ceased to be joint family property. Since the succession opened and the partition took place before the appellant’s birth in 1994, no interest devolved on him. The bench clarified that Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act and Section 29-A of the Hindu Succession (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act, 1989, which conferred equal coparcenary rights on daughters, had no application. The appellant, being a male, could not claim benefits meant for daughters, and the property had already been transformed into individual ownership through partition. Holding that there was no infirmity in the high court’s judgement, the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal.

briefs.headline: Hegseth unfazed by impeachment push, defends Trump's Iran war as 'necessary'
briefs.bodyText:
Facing a growing push for his impeachment, US secretary of war Pete Hegseth has defended US President Donald Trump's military campaign against Iran under Operation Epic Fury, describing it as "necessary" despite questions over its political and electoral fallout after midterm setback.
He also brushed aside impeachment concerns and urged Republican lawmakers to approve a major military funding package.
Speaking at the Naval War College on Monday (local time), before addressing journalists, Hegseth backed US President Donald Trump's position that he would take military action against Iran again.
"This was a -- it doesn't have to be necessarily popular, but it can be necessary," war secretary said.
His remarks came after a reporter referred to a social media post in which the Vice President reportedly said pollsters considered the Iran war the primary reason behind Republican setbacks in the midterm elections.
Hegseth declined to assign blame or confirm whether he had discussed the post with the Vice President.
"Well, I appreciate the Vice President very much, and I'm not going to get in the middle of a finger-pointing exercise," Hegseth said.
Calling the Vice President an important member of the administration's team, Hegseth said officials were free to share candid feedback internally. He also defended Trump's decision to confront what he described as Iran's pursuit of a nuclear weapon.
Hegseth alleged that Tehran had developed a conventional missile shield to obstruct international efforts to counter its nuclear ambitions. He pointed to Operations Midnight Hammer and Epic Fury as decisive measures taken by the administration in response.
Asked whether Republicans had enough support to defeat articles of impeachment against him that week, Hegseth expressed confidence but declined to disclose any specific vote count.
"Oh, we're not worried about that," he said.
Earlier, Hegseth had dismissed calls for his removal as politically motivated, accusing his critics of undermining successful military operations and the achievements of American service personnel.
He also credited the Trump administration with securing increased financial contributions from European allies, expanding joint operations against Latin American cartels and strengthening partnerships across the Pacific.
While refusing to specify the conditions that would formally bring the Iran war to an end, Hegseth maintained that Trump continued to hold the tactical advantage. He said the president retained the option to halt military operations while warning Tehran against transferring nuclear material.
He said, "Whatever he wants to do is his prerogative, and the War Department is prepared to give him the tools to execute on that."
Hegseth identified military funding as his department's top priority over the next two months and called on Republican lawmakers to unite behind a reconciliation Bill that he described as a historic investment.
The proposed funding priorities include intelligence technology, space capabilities, Iron Dome, munitions and shipbuilding. However, he did not disclose the proposed budgetary allocation or provide a legislative timeline.
Hegseth also announced major reforms to senior military colleges following an evaluation process that lasted nearly 18 months.
He said the changes would place greater emphasis on warfighting, deterring conflicts and ensuring the ability to win wars when necessary.
Trump rallies behind Hegseth
Meanwhile, Trump has also backed war secretary Pete Hegseth amid a push by Republican Representative Thomas Massie to secure a House vote on impeaching the Pentagon chief over his handling of the Iran war and other military operations.
In an unexpected appearance at the White House briefing room on Monday, Trump launched an attack on Massie, hours after the Kentucky Republican introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth and read them out on the House floor.
“Massie is a loser,” Trump said, adding, “He shouldn’t be taking up the time of Congress or the Senate or anything that he’s doing.”
Describing Massie as a “stone cold loser”, Trump also pledged to stand by Hegseth even if the House voted to impeach him.
“Yeah, I’ll stand by,” Trump said. “He won two wars. He was in charge. We all won.”
Trump defended Hegseth's record, crediting him with overseeing successful US military operations in Venezuela and Iran. The US operation in Venezuela resulted in the capture of former leader Nicolas Maduro in January, while the conflict with Iran remains ongoing.
“Really, what has Hegseth done?” Trump said. “He won the war. He was in charge. He won the war in Venezuela, as I said, 48 minutes. It was flawless — nobody killed. And he certainly, I think, won the war in Iran.”

briefs.headline: Who is Stephen Miller, Trump’s new Chief of Staff?
briefs.deck: Stephen Miller, one of U.S. President Donald Trump’s closest aides for decades, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week
briefs.bodyText:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (November 6, 2026) named Stephen Miller, architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new Chief of Staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after Republicans were hammered in the midterms.
Ultra-loyalist Miller, 41, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week. In a post on Truth Social announcing Mr. Miller’s appointment, Mr. Trump described him as “one of my most trusted advisors”.
Who is Stephen Miller
Stephen Miller, a key member of Mr. Trump’s inner circle, is a prominent architect of the administration’s hardline immigration policies. Known for his sharp suits and sunglasses, Miller has been one of Mr. Trump’s closest aides for decades and longest-serving advisers, pushing nativist policies that gelled with the President’s “America First” agenda.
Mr. Miller currently serves as White House Deputy Chief of Staff and though he has a wide-ranging portfolio, he is most closely aligned with the President’s immigration policy and rhetoric on immigration. He is also a former aide to hardliner former Sen. Jeff Sessions, R-Ala., who would go on to serve as Mr. Trump’s first Attorney General.
Early years, part of Trump’s campaign
Mr. Miller was raised in politically liberal Santa Monica, California, but developed a reputation as a combative conservative as a columnist at Duke University’s student newspaper. As a congressional aide in the 2010s, he was an early advocate for restricting immigration at a time when that was not a mainstream position in the Republican Party.
He joined Mr. Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, then served as an advisor and speechwriter in his first 2017-2021 term. After Mr. Trump lost the 2020 election, Mr. Miller founded the conservative advocacy group America First Legal, filing complaints that accused companies such as Nike of discriminating against white people.
His wife, Katie Miller, is a conservative podcaster and former communications aide in Mr. Trump’s first administration.
Immigration crackdown
As Mr. Trump’s Deputy Chief of Staff for policy and homeland security advisor, he was the brains behind the mass deportation programme that defined the first year of the President’s second term.
Mr. Miller is best known for driving the immigration crackdown, setting a target of 3,000 arrests per day — far above levels under previous administrations. He has pushed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to target anybody in the country illegally, not just those with criminal records.
But he faced widespread criticism after the deadly shootings of two protesters by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January — incidents that sparked mass demonstrations.
Also read: Killer agents: on immigration enforcement, Minnesota shootings
Beyond enforcement, Mr. Miller has been a vocal advocate for ending birthright citizenship, and denounced the Supreme Court’s ruling that rejected that proposal as “one of the most destructive and outrageous decisions” in the court’s history.
Mr. Miller announced a ban on “birth tourism” after that ruling, seeking to prevent people from coming to the United States to deliver babies.
He also has been a prominent voice on many of the President’s other priorities, including countering diversity initiatives and targeting transgender rights. He is one of a small group of White House staffers who approve all executive orders, a person familiar with the matter said last year, as per a Reuters report.
Mr. Miller has echoed Mr. Trump’s rhetoric on the war with Iran, saying in the early weeks of the conflict that US and Israeli strikes had wiped out Tehran’s leadership class and military capacity. Later, he touted a ceasefire and said on Fox News in July that some Iranian officials are “desperate” to strike a peace deal.
Mr. Miller has advocated for an aggressive foreign policy in other arenas as well. He declined to rule out military action to acquire Greenland in January and said the U.S. was “running Venezuela” after the capture of former President Nicolas Maduro in January.
Why was Wiles replaced
“I wanted to make a change,” Mr. Trump told reporters at the White House when asked why he named Mr. Miller to replace Ms. Wiles.
“Sometimes in life you have to make moves.”
Mr. Trump’s move was particularly startling as he had repeatedly insisted before the midterms that there was “zero chance” of replacing Ms. Wiles.
But naming the combative Miller was the clearest possible signal from Mr. Trump that the gloves are now off after his brief conciliatory gestures to Democrats in the wake of the Republican midterms collapse.
Also read: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
Reactions to Miller’s appointment
Major figures in Mr. Trump’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement — reeling since the midterms — hailed Mr. Miller’s appointment.
“It’s Miller Time,” posted right-wing journalist Jack Posobiec, referring to a famous slogan for an American beer brand.
White House Communications Director Steven Cheung said Mr. Miller was a “Trump OG, someone who has been with the President since the very beginning.”
On the other hand, Democrats pledged they would fight “every step of the way” against Mr. Miller, who became synonymous with scenes of masked immigration agents committing violence after he backed federal agents who shot and killed two Americans.
“Stephen Miller is the architect of the most barbaric, inhumane policies of this administration. Trump couldn’t have made a worse choice,” Minority Leader Chuck Schumer posted on X.

briefs.headline: Nvidia chief told Donald Trump he did not know Chinese woman was a suspected spy
What Nvidia CEO first told world about the woman he has admitted having an affair with
briefs.deck: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly acknowledged an affair that has raised concerns over his leadership. Following his admission, Nvidia initiated an independent investigation into reports concerning foreign intelligence involvement. Huang expressed remorse for his actions towards his family and colleagues while committing to cooperate with the inquiry. US President Donald Trump commented on the…
briefs.bodyText:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, the Chinese tech executive who was at the centre of a reported Chinese spy plot involving the chipmaker's chief. But before the admission, the Nvidia CEO had pushed back against reports about the pair's relationship, describing their interactions as a normal part of the CEO's job. In an interview with Bloomberg in late October 2026, Jensen Huang said his interactions with Alice Huang were related to Megaspeed, Nvidia’s customer, and were “completely normal and not unusual.” In a statement to ABC News on October 31, 2026, the chip maker also responded to a New York Times report alleging that US intelligence officials had determined that Alice Huang, a top executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed International, was funneling information to Chinese officials in Beijing.
The report, published late October, claimed Alice Huang had developed a "close relationship" with Jensen Huang. She was also pictured with the Nvidia CEO in 2024.
Nvidia's initial response was to frame the interactions as routine business meetings. "Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected," the company's spokesperson then said. "Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job."
The spokesperson further said that Jensen Huang "talks with thousands of customer executives every year." 
The company also addressed the allegations surrounding the reported spy plot, saying it relied on information from US authorities to identify potential threats.
"We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," the spokesperson said.
Nvidia added that it would "often receive updates from the U.S. government regarding parties and entities of concern and always act accordingly."
Jensen Huang admits to affair
The controversy took a significant turn on November 8, when Jensen Huang admitted in a message to Nvidia employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” Huang wrote in the email.
Huang also took responsibility for the personal fallout, saying his family had given him love and support but that he had let them down. He said he hoped his family would heal and that, over time, he could earn back their trust. He also apologised to Nvidia colleagues, the board, partners and shareholders, saying they “deserve better” from him.
Nvidia launches an independent investigation
The same day, Nvidia’s board announced that it was initiating an independent investigation into reports that its founder and CEO had been the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.” A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the inquiry. The board said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised,” while adding that the investigation would examine “all available information.”
Huang has committed to cooperating with the review. Nvidia also expressed confidence in his leadership and said he would continue as CEO.
Donald Trump says FBI is looking into the matter
The controversy has since drawn the attention of US President Donald Trump, who said on November 9 that he had spoken to Jensen Huang and asked whether he knew Alice Huang was allegedly a spy.
Trump said Huang told him he had no knowledge of her alleged intelligence links. “He said, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy,’ and I really believe him,” Trump told reporters at the White House.
Trump also confirmed that the FBI was looking into the matter, saying: “I know the FBI is looking into it,” and added, “I think that he'll be in good shape.”
The president described Huang as an “honorable man” and said he had been surprised by the allegations. The FBI’s involvement, as described by Trump, adds a federal law enforcement dimension to the controversy, separate from Nvidia’s internal board investigation.
Jensen Huang’s admission has also triggered speculation about his marriage to Lori Huang, his wife of more than four decades. Reports have discussed the possibility of a divorce and the potential financial implications given the Nvidia CEO’s vast wealth.
However, there has been no publicly confirmed divorce filing or announcement of a separation. Lori Huang has not publicly commented on the affair. The couple, who married in 1985, have two children.

stories.headline: Kautilya's Arthashastra gets Unesco recognition
stories.deck: Kautilya's Arthashastra has been honored by UNESCO, earning a place on the MOWCAP Regional Register. A rare 16th-century manuscript stored at the Oriental Research Institute of the University of Mysore was digitized, revealing insights into governance, finance, and law. Rediscovered by Rudrapatnam Shamasastry in 1905 and later published in 1909, this recognition celebrates the institute's…
stories.bodyText:
MYSURU: Kautilya's Arthashastra, an ancient treatise on governance and statecraft, has been inscribed on 
Unesco
's prestigious Memory of the World Committee for Asia and the Pacific (MOWCAP) Regional Register. An original 16th-century palm-leaf manuscript of the text, preserved and digitised by Oriental Research Institute (ORI) at University of Mysore, is among the institute's most prized collections.
Announcing the recognition, Unesco noted that the Indian manuscript outlines ancient statecraft, public finance and law. The manuscript has been included under the category 'Ancient Governance, History, and Modern Alignment', according to MOWCAP.
"It is a proud milestone in preserving and celebrating India's timeless intellectual heritage," ORI director D P Madhusudanacharya said.
Manuscript is digitised 
MOWCAP is a Unesco programme that identifies, preserves and promotes documentary heritage of outstanding historical, cultural and intellectual significance in Asia-Pacific region.
Madhusudanacharya said a team of experts from Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, New Delhi, had visited the institute and reviewed the manuscript. 
"This recognition brings great honour to the institute, the University of Mysore and the entire Indian manuscript research community," he siad.
The manuscript was discovered at ORI in 1905 by scholar and librarian Rudrapatnam Shamasastry, who subsequently published the text in 1909.
The discovery brought the ancient Indian treatise back to scholarly attention. The manuscript has since been digitised as part of the institute's conservation efforts.

stories.headline: Marriage and motherhood should not affect career: Karnataka high court
stories.deck: Karnataka high court ruled that marriage and motherhood should not limit a woman's ability to relocate for work. An ophthalmologist was allowed to move to the UK despite her husband's objections regarding custody and travel consent. The court emphasized the importance of financial stability and opportunities for the child in the mother's relocation plans. Conditions were set for parental…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Marriage, motherhood and raising children should not affect a woman's professional career or tie her down to one place, Karnataka high court has observed in a recent judgement, clearing an ophthalmologist's relocation to the United Kingdom.
'Motherhood doesn't confine a woman to single place'
In an order passed on Oct 29, Justice Lalitha Kanneganti disposed of a petition filed by the woman's husband, who resides in Mumbai. He had challenged the order of a Bengaluru family court that directed him to deliver the original passport of their minor child to his wife and provide consent to obtain a visa to travel to the United Kingdom.
He had challenged another order rejecting his request for a change in interim custody of the minor child from the wife's family to his family, along with other consequential relief.
'Motherhood doesn't confine a woman to single place'
The wife argued she had been taking care of the child since 2019 when they were thrown out of their residence in Mumbai. According to her, employment in the UK provides a better and more secure financial position, enabling her to provide the child with stable housing, education, healthcare and extracurricular opportunities.
"Marriage and motherhood do not require her to remain confined to a particular place," the judge said, specifying conditions for mutual visits: The mother shall allow regular audio and video calls between the father and the child at least for 20 minutes a day; the father shall get parenting time with the child during school holidays; twice in a year during the child's holidays, the mother shall send the boy to India to spend 75% of the vacation with the father; the father could go to the United Kingdom to meet the child for 75% of the holidays.

stories.headline: Karnataka High Court issues guidelines to BMRCL for ensuring access to remaining portion of properties acquired for metro project
stories.deck: Court declares some provisions of Way Leave Policy as unconstitutional while imposing costs of ₹10 lakh on corporation
stories.bodyText:
The Karnataka High Court has issued a series of directions to the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) to assess, at the planning stage itself, how land acquisition for metro projects will affect the remaining portions of the acquired properties instead of forcing property owners to seek remedies for access after acquisition.
The court has also declared as unconstitutional certain provisions of the BMRCL’s Way Leave Policy (WLP) that permits it to discontinue a way-leave facility at any time without notice, together with provisions excluding compensation, refund or alternative access upon such discontinuance.
Landlocked property
Justice Suraj Govindaraj passed the order while partly allowing a petition filed by M/s Ellis Fashion Exports Private Limited, whose commercial property on Bannerghatta Road was left landlocked after the BMRCL acquired its road-facing frontage for the Jayadeva Hospital Metro Station.
The court has also imposed costs of ₹10 lakh on the BMRCL for compelling the petitioner to opt for litigation while directing it to provide on a permanent basis, free of cost and without an agreement for a fixed term, the ingress and egress to the petitioner’s property.
Also, the court has declared as unconstitutional “the charging provisions in clause 4 of WLP for passages wider than 3.5 metres to landlocked properties, and relating to electricity lines and water or sewage pipelines serving the remaining property... and the requirements for 10 years’ upfront payment and revision or renewal of charges by reference to prevailing guidance value”.
The provisions declared as unconstitutional should not be applied to owners whose original access or frontage has been lost because of the BMRCL’s acquisition for the metro project, the court clarified.
Further, the court directed that where acquisition is likely to leave the property without effective access or essential services, the BMRCL must inspect the site, consult the affected owner, and consider a workable arrangement before the existing access or services are disrupted. The assessment and proposed solution must be recorded in writing, the court said.
Acquire remaining portion
“If the BMRCL considers that effective replacement access cannot reasonably be provided, it must communicate its reasons to the affected owner and consider, in accordance with law, whether acquisition of the remaining property or another lawful solution is appropriate,” the court said.
The owners whose property has been left without access “should not be kept indefinitely in uncertainty”, the court clarified.
Where utility routes are affected, the court said, the BMRCL must coordinate with service providers and the affected owner to identify a workable arrangement for continuity or restoration of essential services without delay. Administrative or contractual conditions shall not be imposed in a manner that defeats the practical provision of essential services.
The court directed the BMRCL’s managing director to issue internal instructions to ensure compliance with these directions, while making it clear that the impact of acquisition for the remaining portion of the property must be considered at the planning and implementation stages, and that requests for replacement access by property owners must receive individual consideration.

briefs.headline: Not a Delhi yet: Bengaluru air quality 25% worse than last Deepavali
briefs.deck: Bengaluru experienced a notable increase in the Air Quality Index after the Deepavali fireworks celebrations. The AQI rose from 53 on Saturday to 129 by Monday, moving from satisfactory to moderate. Various areas in the city reported alarming pollution levels, with certain locations exceeding the poor category. Experts highlight the health risks posed by fine particles from fireworks and traffic…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: 
Deepavali
 fireworks that lit up the sky on Sunday night came with a heavy price: Bengaluru’s Air Quality Index (AQI) jumped from 53 on Saturday to 129 on Monday, pushing it from the ‘satisfactory‘ to the ‘moderate‘ category.
It’s a poor consolation Bengaluru is not as bad as Delhi, whose air quality hit a peak of 370. Compared to Deepavali celebrations in 2025, Bengaluru recorded a nearly 25% increase in AQI on the first day of the festival, with the reading rising from 82 (satisfactory) last year to 102 (moderate) at midnight on Sunday this year.
The AQI continued climbing through the night, rising 3-4 points every hour before peaking to 133 around noon on Monday.
What changed in 1 year
Data from Air Quality Portal of Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) shows that Bengaluru’s AQI remained largely stable through the first week of Nov, fluctuating between 53 and 74 after touching 91 on Nov 1.
According to the data recorded by CPCB at 8am Monday, right after the festival night, KSR railway station (Majestic) recorded the worst air quality in the city — an AQI of 228 — with PM10 as the dominant pollutant, placing it in the ‘poor‘ category.
Silk Board, one of most congested junctions, recorded 152 based on PM2.5 levels, while Hombegowdanagar registered 139 and Jayanagar 5th Block recorded 135. Hebbal, a traffic corridor, reported an AQI of 121.
The recorded data showed that Bengaluru’s overall AQI stood at 74 on Sunday at 8pm, when the permitted cracker-bursting window began.
It touched 85 by 10pm, when the official window closed. However, the AQI began worsening thereafter, crossing 93 by 11pm. By midnight, it had breached the 100 mark to touch 102, moving from the ‘satisfactory’ to the ‘moderate’ category.
The fact that Bengaluru’s wind and rain help disperse pollutants faster than in other cities, should not be seen as a lack of impact.
“Fine particles released from crackers and other combustion sources remain harmful to human health, especially for those living or travelling near busy traffic corridors,” said air-pollution expert Dr Manisha Mishra, assistant professor at Azim Premji University.
Forest, environment and ecology minister Ramalinga Reddy told TOI pollution levels were relatively low in 2025 because it had rained and fewer people chose to burst crackers. “Police (who had the mandate) should have cracked down on those bursting crackers beyond the permitted hours,” he said.
Karnataka State Pollution Control Board chairperson B Shivanna said if restrictions are strictly enforced, many will “brand us anti-tradition or anti-religious, arguing that they burst crackers only once a year.
Unlike water pollution, where we can identify specific sources, the entire city is responsible for this, and we cannot blame any one person.”

briefs.headline: Bengaluru: Firecracker injuries threaten vision; two infants among victims
briefs.deck: At the State-run Minto Ophthalmic Hospital, 12 of the 20 patients treated over the three days till November 9 suffered grievous injuries.
briefs.bodyText:
Firecracker-related eye injuries continue to take the sparkle out of the festival of lights, with several people facing the risk of partial or near-total vision loss this Deepavali too. Children, including infants as young as three and five months, are among those affected, while bystanders account for a significant share of the victims.
Bystanders bear the brunt
At the State-run Minto Ophthalmic Hospital, 12 of the 20 patients treated over the three days till November 9 suffered grievous injuries. Significantly, 13 were bystanders who were watching others burst crackers or happened to be nearby. The remaining seven were injured while bursting crackers themselves.
The cases included 10 male and two female patients, apart from eight children. A 12-year-old boy from Doddaballapur suffered a ruptured eyeball after being hit by a firecracker burst by another person and is at risk of partial vision loss. Eight patients sustained minor injuries, while 12 suffered grievous injuries. Four have been admitted, with two requiring surgery. Doctors said the extent of vision loss could be assessed only after three to six months.
Bijili crackers accounted for six injuries, while five patients could not identify the crackers responsible. Other cases involved flower pots, bombs, Lakshmi crackers and rockets.
Narayana Nethralaya, across its Rajajinagar, Bommasandra, Bannerghatta Road and Whitefield centres, reported 60 patients between November 6 and 9, including 30 children below 18 years and 15 bystanders. One patient required surgery, while the others were managed medically.
Naren Shetty, Director of the Rajajinagar centre, expressed concern over the high proportion of children among the injured and urged parents to supervise them and ensure they maintain a safe distance while bursting crackers.
Infants among those injured
Sankara Eye Hospital documented 26 firecracker-related injury cases till November 9, involving patients aged between three months and 46 years. Its records included three-month-old and five-month-old infants among those who suffered injuries.
Thermal and chemical burns, blunt trauma, corneal abrasions and eyelid injuries were among the commonly reported injuries. One patient suffered a globe rupture and required evisceration with orbital implant placement, doctors said.
At Nethradhama Super Speciality Eye Hospital, a nine-year-old boy sustained a right-eye injury after a firecracker exploded near him while he was standing in a park. Brought to the hospital within 10 to 15 minutes, his vision was initially limited to hand movements. Doctors diagnosed hyphema (bleeding inside the eye) and elevated intraocular pressure.
“Timely intervention was crucial, as delay could have caused permanent vision loss. He is currently doing much better and has been advised to continue treatment,” said Raksha Jagdishprasad Vaishnav, Surgeon – Cataract and Glaucoma at the hospital.
Use protective eyewear
Doctors said most firecracker-related eye injuries are preventable and urged people to exercise caution during celebrations. Children should never be allowed to handle firecrackers without adult supervision and must be kept at a safe distance from the point of ignition. Protective eyewear, preferably shatter-resistant glasses, should be worn not only by those bursting crackers but also by family members and bystanders watching nearby.
They also cautioned against holding lit firecrackers in one’s hand or attempting to relight crackers that fail to ignite. In the event of an eye injury, people should not rub or apply pressure to the affected eye or try home remedies. Instead, they should seek immediate medical attention from an ophthalmologist, as timely treatment can help prevent further damage and improve the chances of preserving vision.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru serial murders: Remaining 2 bodies recovered from Shiradi Ghat
briefs.deck: SLUG: SERIAL KILLINGS
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A multi-state search operation following the Rajajinagar serial murders reached a major breakthrough Monday afternoon with the recovery of the remaining two missing bodies from the dense forest ravines of Shiradi Ghat near Hassan. The victims were identified as Shankar and his wife, Nalini. Police dispatched the bodies to a hospital in Hassan for post-mortem examinations and DNA tests.
Deputy commissioner of police (north division), BS Nemagoud, said the investigators are now transitioning to the procedural phase of the case.
“All seven bodies have been recovered and we will swiftly start working on taking detailed statements from the accused and others,” he said.
Over the course of four days, search teams traversed steep terrain, forests and state lines to locate the scattered remains.
On Friday morning, the search commenced at the foothills of Nandi Hills in Chikkaballapur, where police recovered the body of seven-year-old Puneeth.
The next day, the investigators located the remains of Indushekhar’s wife Sunitha and her mother Rupavathi, discarded in the Yercaud forests of Salem, Tamil Nadu.
Two more bodies, identified as Shivakumar and his wife Divya, were retrieved near the forest trails of Chamundi hills in Mysuru Sunday afternoon.
Forensic inspection revealed a calculated and uniform method used to wrap and transport the victims. All seven bodies were found tightly wrapped in old household cloths, including saris and bedsheets, encased in heavy plastic sheeting and tightly bound with multiple ropes.
To cover up the smell of decomposition during transport, the main accused, identified as cab driver Indushekhar, regularly sprayed perfume inside his Toyota Etios. He used the vehicle on different dates to transport the bodies, the investigation revealed.
The mass murder, allegedly executed over a fortnight at a Rajajinagar home, came to light after Thungamma, Nalini’s mother, filed a complaint after family members repeatedly failed to answer phone calls.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru woman, lover arrested for killing man, faking heart attack
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 In a murder case that initially appeared to be an accidental death, Electronics City police arrested two persons -- the deceased man’s wife and her lover -- for allegedly conspiring to murder Upendra N, 41, and staging his death as a heart attack.
The arrested are Anitha, 36, and her lover, Talasani Madhusudhan Reddy, 46, a cab driver.
Upendra and Anitha, who resided at Doddathoguru on Bettadasanapura Main Road, were running a small call centre related to loans in private banks. All three were natives of Sathya Sai district in 
Andhra Pradesh
.
Police were alerted about Upendra’s death by his brother, Rajendra, on Oct 12. When they questioned Anitha, she said Upendra slipped and fell while going to the bathroom and died due to cardiac arrest. However, police noticed bruises on his face and neck and suspected Anitha's involvement.
Based on a complaint filed by Rajendra, police initially registered an unnatural death report (UDR) case. Inspector Azheruddin and his team collected call detail records of Upendra and Anitha and monitored her movements. The postmortem report said it was “death was due to asphyxia as a result of throttling, mode of compression to be investigated”.
Cops verified CCTV footage from cameras installed around Upendra’s house and gathered crucial information: Anitha would frequently call Reddy and his movements were captured by cameras near the house.
On Nov 5, Reddy was summoned for questioning and he confessed to having a relationship with Anitha. According to him, Upendra used to harass Anitha and warn her repeatedly over the affair. Consequently, Reddy and Anitha decided to murder Upendra.
On the night of Oct 11, Upendra reportedly assaulted Anitha, following which she called Reddy. He reached Upendra’s house around midnight. He found the two children asleep in the hall and Upendra in the bedroom. Reddy told police he sat on top of Upendra and gripped his neck with both hands. Simultaneously, Anitha covered her husband’s face and nose. After struggling for a while, Upendra stopped breathing.
Anitha then asked Reddy to leave, saying she would inform Rajendra that Upendra had slipped and fallen while going to the bathroom, resulting in cardiac arrest.
Police detained Anitha from her residence on Nov 6. During questioning, she also confessed to her involvement in the murder.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru: Shivakumar announces 50% cut in guidance value for regularisation of BDA sites
briefs.deck: ‘The reduction is part of the implementation of Section 38(D) of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, which provides an opportunity for eligible occupants to get their houses regularised by paying the prescribed charges’
briefs.bodyText:
To resolve long-pending property-related grievances, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Monday announced a 50% reduction in the guidance value considered for calculating charges to regularise unauthorised houses built on land acquired by the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA).
Addressing the media after reviewing the BDA’s works, Mr. Shivakumar said that as the BDA completes 50 years, the government wanted to provide relief to those who had been living in houses built on BDA-acquired land for years. This also comes in the backdrop of a lukewarm response from residents who have built houses on these lands. Even as the BDA is estimated to collect nearly ₹5,000 crore through this regularisation scheme, its multiple efforts since 2015 have failed to yield any results.
“The reduction is part of the implementation of Section 38(D) of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, which provides an opportunity for eligible occupants to get their houses regularised by paying the prescribed charges,” he said, adding that the provision was introduced in 2020 to help people who had constructed houses on land acquired by the BDA before July 10, 2008, after the final acquisition notification had been issued.
The scheme was expected to benefit around 1 lakh property owners, but many had not come forward to apply, he said. “We have now reduced these rates to half of what was prescribed under the BJP government’s decision and are giving them (occupants) another opportunity,” he said.
For instance, owners of sites measuring up to 20 ft × 30 ft will have to pay 5% of the current guidance value, down from 10%. For larger sites measuring above 40 ft × 60 ft and up to 50 ft × 80 ft, it has been reduced from 50% to 25%, apart from the applicable penalty. These rates are for sites other than corner sites, for which twice the applicable rates will be charged. The applications will be accepted until December 17.
The application process is currently under way. Applicants will have to submit the prescribed documents, including sale deeds, encumbrance certificates, property tax receipts and Khata documents. The process is to be carried out online. Applicants are required to submit the documents and pay the applicable charges online within two months of receiving a notice.
However, the provision excludes properties situated on land reserved for amenities such as parks, playgrounds and open spaces. It also excludes land connected with national highways and bypass roads. Properties affected by disputes or impediments arising from interim court orders are also excluded.
“Many people have purchased these properties over the years, but they do not have proper legal documents. We wanted to create a provision to provide relief to such property owners. Accordingly, we have reduced the rates and given them another opportunity,” he said, warning that the BDA would be compelled to initiate legal action against those who continued to occupy the land without getting their properties regularised.

briefs.headline: Boy drowns in resort swimming pool near Ramanagar in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A three-and-a-half-year-old boy drowned in the swimming pool of a resort in Ramanagara Monday afternoon. The victim is Lan Ghongindhanj Dhongloi, whose parents, Luminlen Chongloi and Tracy, are from 
Manipur
 and work in private firms in Bengaluru.
Police said around 50 Manipuris had come to Ravishing Retreat resort located on Machanabele Road in Harisandra Monday morning. They had opted for a ‘day in-day out’ package.
A police officer said: “Post-lunch, there was a group photo session near one of the swimming pools. Dhongloi, who was playing nearby, went near the pool and accidentally slipped in. Unfortunately, no one noticed him then. Sometime later, one of the group members saw the boy in the water and alerted others. Though he was shifted to a nearby hospital, doctors declared him dead.”
There was no attendant near the swimming pool when the tragedy took place, the police officer added.

stories.headline: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
stories.deck: October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait
stories.bodyText:
The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel tracking data showed.
* Last month, 31 LNG tankers went through the key waterway, according to data from S&P Global Energy, of which 23 were loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island in the United Arab Emirates.
* October exports were the highest since February when the war started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait, the data showed.
* “We are looking at UAE back to pre-war transit levels and Qatar at over 30% of pre-war Hormuz transits,” said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at S&P Global Energy.
* Kpler’s shiptracking data showed 42 LNG cargoes were loaded in October, up from 27 in September.
* The changes come as Ras Laffan’s October loadings reached 35 cargoes, surpassing 2.7 million tons, the highest since the war started, according to Kpler data. Qatar exported nearly 6.2 million tons in February.
* Two of the vessels carrying LNG from Ras Laffan that exited the strait subsequently conducted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers off the coast of Oman’s Sohar anchorage, Kpler data showed. The SC Prestige transferred LNG to the BW ENN Crystal Sky, which is now bound for South Korea.
* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.
* Das Island exports held steady at seven loadings in October, flat with September, Kpler data showed.

stories.headline: Stock market today: Are NSE, BSE open or closed on November 10 for Diwali-Balipratipada?
stories.deck: With the festive season bringing changes to the regular trading calendar, investors may be wondering whether the stock market will remain open or closed today, Tuesday, November 10. Following a special Muhurat trading session on Sunday and a regular session on Monday, both the BSE and NSE will remain closed today on account of Diwali-Balipratipada. Regular trading will resume on Wednesday…
stories.bodyText:
The festive season has brought changes to the regular trading schedule, with Indian stock exchanges observing holidays around Diwali. After a special 
Muhurat Trading
 session on Sunday and a regular trading session on Monday, investors may be looking to resume trading on Tuesday, November 10.
According to the 2026 holiday calendar of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), will remain closed on account of Diwali-Balipratipada. The holiday applies to the equity, equity derivatives and securities lending and borrowing (SLB) segments, among other market segments.
Sensex and Nifty ended higher on Monday, recovering after marginally slipping in the special Muhurat trading session on Sunday. The Sensex rose 107.25 points, or 0.13 per cent, to 81,106.65, while the Nifty gained 58.25 points, or 0.23 per cent, to reclaim the 25,000 mark at 25,044.65. Buying in banking and financial stocks, along with a decline in crude oil prices, supported the benchmarks, although losses in IT and metal shares capped gains. Brent crude fell 1.04 per cent to $97.46 per barrel.
Also read: 
Are banks open or closed on November 10, 2026? Check state-wise list
Are NSE and BSE closed?
Yes. Both the NSE and BSE will remain closed on Tuesday, November 10, for Diwali-Balipratipada.
Trading will remain suspended across the equity, equity derivatives and SLB segments. The capital market, derivatives market, electronic gold receipts (EGR) and debt market will also remain closed.
The exchanges will resume normal trading on Wednesday, November 11, with the regular equity market session scheduled from 9:15 am to 3:30 pm.
Meanwhile, the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) will remain closed during the morning session, from 9 am to 5 pm. However, trading will resume in the evening session from 5 pm to 11:30 pm.
The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX), meanwhile, will remain closed for the entire day.
The exchanges have declared November 10 a trading holiday on account of Diwali-Balipratipada, also known as Bali Pratipada. The festival is observed on the day after Diwali and marks the annual return of King Mahabali to his kingdom, according to Hindu mythology.
The holiday follows the special Muhurat Trading session held on Sunday, November 8, to mark the beginning of Samvat 2083, the Hindu financial year. The exchanges subsequently conducted a regular trading session on Monday, November 9.
After the November 10 closure, the next scheduled trading holiday for the NSE and BSE is November 24, Tuesday, on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev.
The exchanges will also remain closed on December 25 for Christmas, according to their 2026 holiday calendars, apart from the regular weekend holidays.

stories.headline: Oil prices edge lower as Trump signals pause in military action against Iran
stories.deck: Oil prices decreased following US President Donald Trump's comments regarding military action against Iran. Although Trump postponed military strikes, he stated that the naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz would continue. Oil production by Opec rose in October due to increased output from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Iraq. Russian and Ukrainian officials held peace talks aimed at resolving the…
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday, extending the previous session's losses, after US President Donald Trump said military action against Iran was not necessary “at this point”. His remarks eased concerns over prolonged disruptions to oil supplies from the Middle East.
Brent crude futures fell 24 cents, or 0.23%, to $92.33 a barrel by 0102 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 35 cents, or 0.40%, to $86.50 a barrel.
Brent had settled 5.85% lower in the previous session after falling to its lowest level since August 31.
Trump signals pause in strikes, but Hormuz blockade to continue
Trump said on Monday that he planned to hold off on fresh military strikes against Iran for the time being, following appeals from countries in the region. These included an appeal from Qatar's prime minister during talks at the White House.
In an interview with Reuters and a subsequent appearance in the White House briefing room, Trump said the US would maintain its naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now.
“The market continues to prioritise President Trump's more conciliatory tone toward Iran since the midterms,” said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.
He added that attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz were continuing but had not escalated enough to bring a fresh risk premium into the market.
However, senior US and Gulf officials have expressed doubts about the possibility of an imminent peace deal between Washington and Tehran.
Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei rejected reports of negotiations, saying the US should “stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks”.
He added that it was “time to surrender to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out”.
Opec output rises, Russia-Ukraine talks in focus
On the supply side, oil production by the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (Opec) increased in October, according to a Reuters survey. The rise was led by higher output in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq, despite continued constraints on exports.
Elsewhere, Russian and Ukrainian officials were scheduled to meet on Tuesday for two days of US-brokered talks. The meeting would be their first since February.
Trump had suggested last week that a broader peace agreement could be possible in the 4.5-year-old Russia-Ukraine war and could also incorporate Europe's security.

stories.headline: Nvidia plunges but tech shares rebound, oil prices slump
stories.deck: Nvidia shares slumped more than 8% as trading got under way in New York but recovered to stand down more than 5% in early afternoon trading
stories.bodyText:
Technology share prices clawed back last week's sharp losses on Monday (November 9, 2026), despite a plunge in Nvidia following a probe into its boss Jensen Huang over claims of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Oil prices fell over 5% on hopes for diplomatic talks aimed at ending the U.S.-Iran war, before paring losses.
Chipmakers and other companies linked to the artificial intelligence boom took a hammering in the days after last Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections, which saw Democrats sweep both chambers of Congress, leading to speculation lawmakers would seek to rein in tech firms.
But Wall Street on Monday (November 9, 2026) rebounded, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq climbing more than 2%.
Briefing.com analyst Patrick O'Hare said the rebound in equities was due to more than just the drop in oil prices.
"What we also have this morning is an inclination to buy into last week's weakness, and specifically into the large losses seen in the AI trade," he said in a note to clients.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which includes major chipmakers and AI firms, jumped more than 6%.
But the gains did not extend to Nvidia, which saw its shares slump more than 8% as trading got under way in New York, but recovered to stand down more than 5% in early afternoon trading.
Mr. O'Hare said Nvidia was being treated as a one-off story by investors for the moment.
"In other words, the stock is being penalized for Jensen Huang's personal transgression, which has invited a great deal of uncertainty into the mix, but the market isn't caught up in the notion that this situation is going to have a systemic domino effect," he said.
The news that Nvidia's board would investigate whether Mr. Huang had been targeted in a foreign espionage plot, following his admission he was unfaithful to his wife, brought fresh uncertainty in the markets.
The New York Times last month reported that U.S. intelligence officials concluded a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed had been funnelling information to Beijing.
The executive, Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Mr. Jensen Huang — developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said.
In a message to company employees released to media on Sunday (November 8, 2026), Mr. Huang acknowledged having an affair and apologised to his family and company staff.
Nvidia is a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models and one of the world's most valuable companies, and last year became the first to reach a market capitalisation of $5 trillion.
Technology analyst Dan Ives, at the investment bank Yorkville Ives, said the crisis would at the very least spark congressional inquiries and "create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons".
China on Monday (November 9, 2026) said the claims that it had spied on Mr. Huang were "baseless".
Europe's main stock markets rose following gains across much of Asia.
The dollar fell against its main rivals.
Oil prices continued to slide as Iran and the United States continued talking instead of fighting.
"Two month lows in oil have done much to bolster bruised sentiment in global markets, and the admittedly small signs of progress in peace talks adds to downward move," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at online trading and investing platform IG.
