briefs.headline: Are banks open or closed on November 10 for Diwali (Bali Pratipada)? Check state-wise list
briefs.deck: On November 10, select bank branches across India will be closed in observance of Diwali, a time for festive celebrations. While customers can still enjoy digital banking options like mobile banking and UPI, in-person services at physical branches will be unavailable. Additionally, due to various local festivals, some regions will also experience bank closures on November 11.
briefs.bodyText:
Amid the festive season, bank holidays across the country continue to vary by state, with several regions observing local festivals and religious occasions. With Diwali celebrations extending into this week, many customers may be wondering whether banks will remain open or closed on Tuesday, November 10.
According to the 
Reserve Bank of India
's (RBI) holiday calendar, banks in select states will observe a holiday on account of Diwali (Bali Pratipada), also known as Govardhan Puja and Vikram Samvat New Year Day. Govardhan Puja commemorates Lord Krishna lifting the Govardhan hill to protect villagers from torrential rains, while Bali Pratipada marks the annual return of King Mahabali to his kingdom, according to Hindu mythology. The day also marks the beginning of the Hindu New Year in Gujarat, known as Bestu Varas or Vikram Samvat New Year.
The holiday applies to certain cities and regions, rather than the entire country.
Where are banks closed on November 10?
As per the RBI's November 2026 holiday calendar, bank branches will remain closed in the following cities on Tuesday:
- Gujarat: Ahmedabad
- Maharashtra: Mumbai, Nagpur and Belapur
- Karnataka: Bengaluru
- Uttarakhand: Dehradun
- Sikkim: Gangtok
The closures are observed under the Negotiable Instruments Act. Bank holidays in India vary across states and regions depending on local festivals and observances.
Can you access banking services today?
Although physical bank branches will remain closed in the regions observing the holiday, customers can continue to access most banking services through digital channels.
Internet banking, mobile banking, UPI and ATM services are generally available on bank holidays. Customers can use these platforms for fund transfers, bill payments, balance enquiries and cash withdrawals.
However, services requiring a physical branch visit, including certain cheque-related transactions and other in-person banking operations, may be affected.
When will banks remain closed next this month?
According to the RBI's holiday calendar, banks in select regions will also remain closed on Wednesday, November 11, for Laxmi Puja (Deepawali), Ningol Chakkouba, Bhratridwitiya, Bhaidooj and Chitragupt Jayanti.
The holiday will apply to Gangtok in Sikkim, Imphal in Manipur, Kanpur and Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh, Kolkata in West Bengal, and Shimla in Himachal Pradesh.
[Source: RBI]

briefs.headline: L&T bags ₹1,000 - ₹2,500 crore order from Noida Metro Rail Corporation for Aqua Line extension
briefs.bodyText:
Infrastructure major Larsen & Toubro (L&T) on Monday (November 9, 2026) said it has secured an order ranging between ₹1,000 crore and ₹2,500 crore from Noida Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.
The scope of the project covers the part design and construction of a 15.1-km elevated viaduct from Botanical Garden to Noida Sector-142 and from the Depot Station to Boraki, along with the construction of 10 elevated metro stations, including architectural finishes.
The order has been bagged by L&T's heavy civil infrastructure business vertical for the part design and construction of the Noida Metro Aqua Line Extension Project, the company said in a statement.
Noida Metro Aqua Line Extension is poised to become a landmark urban transit project, significantly enhancing regional connectivity and commuter accessibility. The project will play a crucial role in supporting Noida's expanding urban landscape. It is scheduled to be completed within a stringent 36-month timeline, the statement added.
Larsen & Toubro is a $32-billion Indian multinational engaged in engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) projects, hi-tech manufacturing, products and services, operating across diverse domains and multiple geographies.

briefs.headline: Meta sets India pricing for Muse AI agent ahead of launch
briefs.deck: It is unclear when Meta’s rapidly growing Muse AI agent will launch in India; however, the service already displays pricing in Indian rupees.
briefs.bodyText:
Meta has set rupee-denominated subscription prices for its rapidly growing AI agent, Muse, ahead of its official launch in India.
The service is priced at ₹1,799 for its Power tier and ₹8,999 for the Maximum tier, with marginally higher charges for subscriptions purchased through Google Play and Apple’s billing systems, The Hindu has found. The pricing, which is broadly in line with U.S. rates, has not been reported previously.
It remains unclear whether these prices are final or could be revised when Muse officially launches in India. Meta did not respond to The Hindu’s queries.
AI agents such as Muse and its rival Instinct have gained considerable traction as users increasingly entrust autonomous systems with online tasks. Muse, which allows users to interact with it on WhatsApp, clocked more than 10 million downloads within two months of its launch.
Its applications range from handling customer-service interactions and filling out online forms to planning travel and booking flight tickets.
Muse’s integration with WhatsApp could give it a significant distribution advantage in India, where the messaging platform has a massive user base. The service currently offers a free tier with generous usage limits in the U.S., Canada, Japan and Singapore.
Its San Francisco-based competitor, Instinct, which also operates through WhatsApp, is available globally without a paid subscription tier.
Limited access in India
Although Muse currently places Indian users on a waitlist, users can register through a VPN connected to one of its supported markets. Registered accounts continue to work in India even after users stop routing their internet connections through those countries.
Despite the absence of Muse from Indian app marketplaces, its web and WhatsApp interfaces are accessible in the country. Indian-issued cards can also be used to purchase subscriptions, provided their billing territory is set to a supported market.
However, the service’s functionality in India remains restricted. It does not accept user authorisation to make card payments on their behalf, as this capability depends on integrations with payment processors that do not operate in India.
An executive at a major Indian payment gateway provider, which has worked on agentic payments, denied last month that the company was working with Muse’s developers to integrate such capabilities.
Agents spread online
While personal AI agents such as Muse have not triggered the same level of cybersecurity concerns as unreleased frontier models such as Anthropic’s Mythos, they raise a different set of regulatory and technological questions.
Officials have expressed concerns that advanced frontier models could potentially expose vulnerabilities and trigger data breaches across government and corporate networks. AI agents, meanwhile, throw up a different question: should autonomous digital agents be treated as human users when accessing online services?
The issue could have significant implications for Indian websites that rely on legacy bot-detection technologies such as CAPTCHAs. Agents such as Muse and Instinct can be configured to solve these tests with relative ease.

briefs.headline: BDR Pharma to acquire stake in Acme’s oral solid formulations business
briefs.bodyText:
BDR Pharma will acquire a controlling stake in the oral solid formulations business of Acme Formulation and its subsidiaries from its existing shareholders, led by alternative investment firm PAG.
The transaction values the business at $250 million, a person in the know of the deal said.
BDR Pharma said a key rationale for the acquisition is the addition of complementary capabilities across thyroid products, female sex hormone products and general pharmaceutical products. It aligns with its growth priorities across oncology, critical care and women’s healthcare, while creating opportunities to expand its product offerings in international markets, the company said.
“Acme will further strengthen our CDMO platform and add differentiated capabilities. We see this as part of a larger growth roadmap... as we continue to build and expand our global presence”, said Dharmesh Shah, Chairman and Managing Director of BDR Pharma.
Post sale of the controlling stake in the oral solid business, PAG and Viral Shah will retain full ownership of Immacule, which is a sterile injectable focused contract manufacturing businesses. Immacule had recently commissioned a new facility with a capacity of 200 million units and provides capabilities across dosage forms and in various therapeutic areas.
“BDR Pharma’s strength in new and complex medicines will bring more innovative products to Acme’s CMO and CDMO clients, existing and new, across geographies,” Acme founder and Immacule Managing Director Viral Shah said.

briefs.headline: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
briefs.deck: The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.
briefs.bodyText:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.
“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.
With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

briefs.headline: Nvidia crisis: Will probe into Jensen Huang benefit Indian stock market?
briefs.deck: The development has plunged the US chipmaker, a key player in the global artificial intelligence industry, into an unprecedented crisis. The company also lacks a clearly identified successor to its chief executive. The more serious concern is the allegation that Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
briefs.bodyText:
Nvidia, one of the most valuable listed companies in the world, is in the eye of the storm with the company launching an investigation into reports that its chief executive, Jensen Huang, had been the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.” Nvidia shares dropped 8% at the start of trading on Monday.
Nvidia's processors are widely used in data centres and computing infrastructure that train and operate AI models. Its most advanced chips have also come under the spotlight because of US export curbs designed to restrict China's access to cutting-edge semiconductor technology.
What has happened
Nvidia announced the probe on Sunday, following Huang's admission that he had been intimate with a business executive whom US intelligence agencies had reportedly identified as someone collecting information for China, according to The New York Times.
The New York Times identified Alice Huang as a former executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data centre company whose website prominently highlights its partnership with Nvidia.
Nvidia ranks among the world's most valuable publicly listed companies, alongside Apple and Microsoft. Its chip sales to China have periodically faced restrictions from US regulators seeking to curb Beijing's access to advanced technology.
“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy according to AP report.
“Those questions require evidence rather than speculation,” he added in a text message to reporters.
In recent years, Huang has pressed Washington to ease restrictions on Nvidia's chip exports to China. This year, he secured US President Donald Trump's approval to sell the company's H200 chips to the country. However, it remains uncertain whether Beijing will permit Chinese companies to purchase these processors in substantial volumes.
In a regulatory filing in August, Nvidia disclosed that it had sold only a limited quantity of chips to China, citing restrictions imposed by the Chinese government on such purchases.
Although the H200 is not among Nvidia's most advanced chip models, it remains a sophisticated processor. Huang had earlier also lobbied Trump for permission to sell the company's less advanced H20 chips, which were specifically designed to comply with US export restrictions on China.
China's Foreign Ministry rejected the espionage allegations on Monday, describing them as a smear campaign directed at Beijing.
The development has plunged the US chipmaker, a key player in the global artificial intelligence industry, into an unprecedented crisis.
The company also lacks a clearly identified successor to its chief executive.
The more serious concern is the allegation that Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
Nvidia's board has launched an investigation and maintained that it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.”
The controversy has surfaced at a particularly difficult moment for the company.
Democrats secured control of Congress last week, while candidates advocating closer oversight of artificial intelligence and data-centre construction recorded significant victories.
Nvidia was already facing the possibility of tougher congressional scrutiny over whether its advanced chips were reaching China. The latest allegations involving Huang have given lawmakers from both parties further grounds to examine the company.
Does it impact India?
One would assume that an internal probe in a tech giant in the US would have no impact whatsoever on Indian stock markets.
But, Sensex and Nifty which have delivered negative returns in the last year may actually benefit indirectly from this development. Globally stock markets have rallied on the artificial intelligence and chip-led boom with Nvidia actually leading the rally.
India on the other hand has missed out on the AI stock boom, one of the major factors cited for exit of foreign investors from the stock market.
But after months of underperformance, Indian equities have recently regained investor interest as concerns grow over concentrated investments in AI. Investors are increasingly looking towards factors such as lower crude oil prices and robust domestic corporate earnings. Last week, India emerged as one of Asia's most prominent beneficiaries of the so-called anti-AI trade.
The positive sentiment towards Indian equities received another boost on Monday, with two more banks turning bullish on the market. HSBC upgraded Indian stocks to overweight from neutral, while Citigroup increased its 12-month target for the Nifty 50.
Nvidia is at the heart of the AI investment boom and has increasingly relied on its own balance sheet and credit strength to support faster infrastructure spending.
Bloomberg Opinion columnist Shuli Ren has described Huang as the “central banker of AI.” The question she raises is particularly relevant now: Will Nvidia's money keep flowing now that the central banker himself is in trouble?
According to a Bloomberg analysis, while Huang's troubles alone are not a sufficient basis for an investment case for India, but if the controversy deepens doubts about the AI trade and prompts investors to diversify beyond it, Indian equities could benefit from an unusual advantage that the country does not have a giant, expensive AI sector.
(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

briefs.headline: Jensen Huang's affair with 'Chinese spy': Nvidia stock price plunges 8% amid nvestigation
briefs.deck: Nvidia said an independent committee of its directors would supervise the investigation, with assistance from external independent legal counsel. It was reported last month that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, had developed a close relationship with the Nvidia chief and allegedly passed information directly to Beijing.
briefs.bodyText:
Nvidia shares plunged over 8% in opening trade on Monday after an internal investigation was announced into whether chief executive Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation triggered concerns about his future at the AI chipmaker. Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company.
Earlier today, Nvidia shares dropped 5% in premarket trading. Huang is facing a board-level investigation into whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence operation. The inquiry follows a media report linking him to a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to Beijing.
Last month, The New York Times reported that Huang had been in a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who is not related to him. US authorities investigated her and concluded that she was an asset of Chinese intelligence.
What it means for the stock
According to Bernstein, the controversy is unlikely to dent demand for Nvidia's products.
The allegations could become a "heavy distraction" for the company or, in a worst-case scenario, provide "significant ammunition" to lawmakers from both political parties, brokerage Bernstein said on Monday.
However, the firm warned that regulatory risks could increase as the expansion of AI infrastructure becomes a more prominent political issue. 
The latest developments are also likely to keep Nvidia at the centre of the debate.
Bernstein maintains an "outperform" rating on Nvidia, with a price target of $400.
Nadia El Bilassy, senior market analyst at Equiti Group told Reuters, “This was just the cherry on top for investors looking to pull out of AI-linked stocks. It's a very bad headline that's affecting tech stocks.”
The attention on Nvidia could ease later this week "when we have more important things to discuss, like the inflation data," she added.
Nvidia's technology has featured prominently in several major developments in the tech industry, from video gaming and self-driving vehicles to cloud computing and artificial intelligence.
The company made early investments in AI under Huang's leadership. When ChatGPT was launched in late 2022, Nvidia's chips were already well placed to benefit from the sharp increase in demand for computing power to support AI.
Nvidia has since grown into one of the world's most valuable businesses and a key supplier to major technology companies. Its valuation surged from $420 billion in late 2022 to $4.5 trillion as of November 6.
Separately, US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing company that buys Nvidia products, over suspicions that it helped Beijing obtain advanced AI chips from Nvidia despite restrictions prohibiting their shipment to China.
The New York Times reported last month that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, had developed a close relationship with the Nvidia chief and allegedly passed information directly to Beijing.
Nvidia said an independent committee of its directors would supervise the investigation, with assistance from external independent legal counsel.
The company also said Huang fully supports the review and has pledged to cooperate with the investigation.

briefs.headline: Your meal cost is set to rise: Eggs and chicken prices may rise 25-30% by December
briefs.deck: Wholesale egg prices, currently hovering at Rs 6-7 per egg, are projected to climb to Rs 7-8 by December. The wholesale rate of dressed chicken without skin is also expected to rise from the current Rs 225-250 per kg to Rs 260-275 per kg over the same period, according to senior industry executives.
briefs.bodyText:
Your meal costs may go up in December as egg and chicken prices could rise by 25-30%. This is because the cost of poultry feed ingredients, including maize and broken rice, has climbed 30-45% over the past month compared with the same period a year ago.
Maize and broken rice prices have doubled in the past year. With farmers and traders holding back maize stocks, the industry that uses the grain as a key raw material expects the upward price trend to continue through December.
Eggs, chicken to get costlier as feed prices go up
Wholesale egg prices, currently hovering at Rs 6-7 per egg, are projected to climb to Rs 7-8 by December. The wholesale rate of dressed chicken without skin is also expected to rise from the current Rs 225-250 per kg to Rs 260-275 per kg over the same period, according to senior industry executives.
December and January are among the busiest months for poultry consumption, with demand typically rising during the Christmas and New Year festivities.
Maize, which cost around Rs 18 per kg last year, is now selling at Rs 34 per kg. Prices were in the range of Rs 26-27 per kg just a month ago, according to an ET report.
Industry participants fear that the rate could reach Rs 40 per kg by December, as intermediaries in the supply chain stockpile the commodity in anticipation of further price increases.
Broken rice has also become significantly more expensive. Its price, which stood at Rs 14-15 per kg around November 2025, has risen to Rs 31-32 per kg. A month ago, it was available at approximately Rs 22-23 per kg, according to trade data.
Industry estimates suggest that a deficient monsoon in Maharashtra and Karnataka, two important kharif maize-producing states, could lead to a 15-16% decline in India's kharif maize output.
"Earlier, whenever prices of maize and rice increased, we used to shift to other cereals like jowar, bajra, ragi etc. However, even these cereals are expensive to use in poultry feed now," KG Anand, general manager of Venkateshwara Hatcheries told the financial daily.
"Although the increase in production costs has been high, we cannot pass the entire increase in costs to the consumers," said Anand.
"This year, we are expecting the production to fall by more than 20% during December and January as farmers are likely to sell younger birds in order to reduce the cost of feeding them," said Anand.
Maize prices have continued to rise amid a growing diversion of the grain towards ethanol production. Rice prices, meanwhile, have been climbing as the deficient monsoon is expected to weigh on output of the kharif paddy crop.

stories.headline: Why Shubman Gill is captaining India for the last time in ODI series
stories.deck: Shubman Gill leads India in his final match of the ODI series against New Zealand at Seddon Park. He will miss the fourth and fifth ODIs due to workload management before the Test series. India are ahead in the series, leading series 2-0. Shreyas Iyer will take over as captain for the final two matches.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Shubman Gill
 is leading India for the final time in the ongoing ODI series against New Zealand. The third ODI at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Tuesday is his last match as both captain and player in the five-match series.
Gill will miss the fourth and fifth ODIs as the BCCI has decided to rest some key players ahead of the two-Test series against New Zealand.
After a two-hour delay due to rain and a wet outfield, India won the toss and elected to bowl in the third ODI. The visitors, who lead the series 2-0, are looking to complete a clean sweep.
The first two matches were also affected by rain. India won the opening ODI in Auckland by five wickets while chasing a revised DLS target of 143 in 22.2 overs.
In the second ODI in Wellington, India were declared winners under the DLS method after rain stopped play with the visitors at 113/7 while chasing 135. India were four runs ahead of the DLS par score at that stage.
Why is Shubman Gill playing his last match of the ODI series?
The BCCI had announced separate squads for the first three and the last two ODIs against New Zealand. The decision was taken to manage the workload of key players ahead of the Test series.
Gill was named captain for the first three ODIs, while 
Shreyas Iyer
 will take charge of the team in the final two matches.
The BCCI also named Iyer as vice-captain for the first three matches and Ishan Kishan as vice-captain for the last two ODIs.
Gill, along with 
KL Rahul
 and some other key players, will not be part of the squad for the remaining two matches. They will get time to prepare for the upcoming Test series.
Tight schedule ahead of India-New Zealand Tests
The fourth and fifth ODIs will be played on November 13 and 15 respectively at Mount Maunganui.
The first Test of the two-match series will begin on November 19 at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.
This leaves the Indian players with just four days between the final ODI and the start of the Test series. The short gap makes workload management important, especially for players expected to feature in both formats.
The two-Test series is also important for India's chances of reaching the World Test Championship final. The team management will want its key players to be fresh and ready for the longer format.

stories.headline: Atiqa Mir produces overtaking masterclass to finish 6th on FIA World Championship debut
stories.deck: In a recovery rarely seen in this Championship, Atiqa put on an overtaking masterclass by making up 16 places in Race 1 and finishing P6, which happened to be also the highest by an Indian this weekend
stories.bodyText:
Indian racing prodigy Atiqa Mir produced a special rearguard performance charging through the field to gain 16 places and finish sixth in the opening race on her FIA Karting World Championship debut here.
The 11-year-old Atiqa, who is the first Indian to be backed by the Formula 1 Academy and competes in the 12-14 age category, is known for giving the more experienced drivers a run for their money. Her craft came to the fore once again in the opening race of the biggest karting competition held over the weekend.
A commendable P6 in a world class field came after a heavy setback in qualifying, where two drivers who had crashed, blocked Atiqa while rejoining the track and ruining her hot lap.
The incident put her down to second last in her group and 83rd out of 87 drivers overall. With only three heat races to make up the places, Atiqa had her task cut out and the gritty girl from Srinagar, representing the Kart Republic team, didn’t let the situation faze her.
Prior to qualifying, Atiqa had zoomed to P3 in the Qualifying Sim Practice Session.
In a recovery rarely seen in this Championship, Atiqa put on an overtaking masterclass by making up 16 places in Race 1 and finishing P6, which happened to be also the highest by an Indian this weekend.
She also jumped 10 places in Race 2 and four in Race 3, tallying a gain of whopping 30 places.
She was up by an overall 43 places and ranked 40 out of 87 drivers in a productive weekend.
In the Super Heat on Sunday, Atiqa started 14th on the grid and made up five places quickly before a crash dropped her down to P16 in difficult weather conditions.
“That was a lot of fun and I got amazing overtaking practice, that is how I treated this weekend after the qualifying disaster. That was out of my control so I took control of what I could and drove my heart out.
"I feel I belong at this level and with a better qualifying, I can fight at the front. I want to thank my sponsors Raise and JK Tyre without whom none of this won’t be possible," said Atiqa reflecting on her weekend.
Atiqa's father Asif Mir, India's first national karting champion, said, "We were looking really strong for a top five result but the qualifying spoilt everything for her. (It was) such a shame as she (had) worked really hard to get up to pace. But what followed surprised even me. She is a gutsy little girl playing with the big boys, I was very impressed."

briefs.headline: India's chess GMs: 100 and counting – Why becoming a GM is now just a tiny step
briefs.deck: With the celebration of 100 Grandmasters in India, Anuj Shrivatri stands as the newest star. While reaching the Grandmaster title is commendable, certain players manipulate rules to safeguard their ratings. Currently, only a few maintain an Elo rating above 2500, exposing the fierce competition. The ongoing scarcity of sponsorship and support for chess talents is a pressing issue, which contrasts…
briefs.bodyText:
When 
Viswanathan Anand
 became a Grandmaster in Coimbatore in 1988, attaining that step used to be a giant step towards professional chess. Now, it’s a footnote. India completing a century of GMs on Sunday — with Anuj Shrivatri being the latest one with a win at the ASEAN Plus in the Philippines on Sunday — should be viewed accordingly.
Though FIDE has lowered the regulations to attain a GM title, the players still have to find shortcuts and easier paths to add the accolade to their CV. These include pulling out, withdrawing and reentering from the pairings of the same tournament multiple times, withdrawing from one tournament in one city and travelling to the other city the next day. All this to protect an Elo drop in a bid to reach Elo 2500. Or playing soft tournaments in Europe.
Becoming a GM is still a task, though, and further progress is even more difficult. Frequent and lucrative tournaments are available only for players above Elo 2650. If you don’t reach Elo 2550 by age 17, that final push is improbable. Though becoming a GM before age 18 is possible, it’s a full-time endeavour with escalating costs and entails huge compromises on academics and social life.
Only 51 of India’s GMs have maintained a rating of more than Elo 2500. 
India’s current rating spread of GMs is from Elo 2763 (Pragg) to Elo 2222 (Saptarshi Roy Choudhary). There are nine GMs in India aged 15-25 who are below the minimum GM rating of Elo 2500, with the lowest being Prithu Gupta at 2398, the India No. 142 and not among 3,000 best players in the world.
When Anand became a GM there were less than 200 active GMs rated above Elo 2500, now there are about 550. And if we count GMs who have slipped below Elo 2500, there are about 750 more GMs the world over. The situation is dramatically better for women who manage to attain GM title after hardships including social and emotional challenges.
“Generally, the players have to pay huge amounts as coaching fees and most of the GMs today are unemployed or unsponsored. There are many others who spend these types of funds but never ever cross the rating of Elo 1900. Private sponsors and funding for coaching is very small in number compared to the aspirants trying to get titles in India,” Pravin Thipsay, former seven-time National champion and coach, told TOI.
“It’s sad that unlike the Soviet Chess Federation or the Russian Chess Federation or Chinese Chess Federation, the AICF has not attempted to create a system wherein the GMs and other merited players would be absorbed for training assignments or for any other form of services by which a player could get reasonable financial benefits,” he added.

briefs.headline: Confidence remains biggest challenge after historic bronze, says Tirthank Pegu
briefs.deck: First Indian male swimmer to win Youth Olympic medal says self-belief could have helped him achieve even better finish
briefs.bodyText:
KOLKATA: Youth Olympic bronze medallist Tirthank Pegu believes a lack of self-belief may have cost him an even higher finish in the 200m butterfly event, admitting that his mindset remains the biggest area of improvement as he targets an unprecedented Olympic final for India.
“The biggest area I need to improve is my mindset. I need to become more positive and more confident in myself,” Pegu said after becoming the first Indian male swimmer to win a medal at the Youth Olympics. “I truly believe my medal could have been a different colour if I hadn’t been struggling with confidence over the past month.”
The 17-year-old from Assam secured bronze in the men’s 200m butterfly in 2:01.25, days after narrowly missing the podium in the 100m butterfly, where he finished fourth in 54.98 seconds, just 0.27 seconds adrift of bronze.
The swimmer admitted that the heartbreak of narrowly missing a medal in the 100m butterfly also affected him before the 200m final. “To be honest, I was really nervous. I was focusing too much on the medal and worrying about disappointing my coach and everyone who supported me,” he said during a virtual interaction on Monday. “During the last 50m, the only thing in my head was, ‘I hope I get a medal’.”
This historic feat would not have been possible though without the influence of his late father, Kunal, a district-level amateur boxer. 
While Kunal wanted his son to take up boxing, Pegu’s mother was worried about injuries to his face. The youngster eventually took to swimming at the age of four, with his father becoming the driving force behind his journey. The road, however, was far from easy.
“It was a struggle financially, but he never showed that struggle to me,” Pegu said. “He did everything he could for my swimming. My mother often says that my father never invested in anything else. I was his investment.”
Though his father is no longer around to celebrate the milestone, Pegu, an athlete of Inspire Institute of Sport, carries his influence with him as he looks towards the next phase of his career.
Pegu’s achievement came shortly after 
Dhinidhi Desinghu
 became the first Indian swimmer to win a Youth Olympic medal, making it a landmark edition of the Games for Indian swimming.
While many have described this as a breakthrough moment, Pegu believes it is the result of years of groundwork laid by earlier generations of swimmers. “I wouldn’t call it a sudden success,” he said. “Dhinidhi had already competed at the Olympics in Paris and swimmers like Sajan Prakash and 
Srihari Nataraj
 showed what was possible. They created the pathway for us.”
For Pegu, the Youth Olympics was the culmination of a year-long effort built around a single target. A large part of his development, according to the teenager, has come under coach Sandeep Sejwal.
With Sejwal set to retire from coaching, the medal also carried added significance for Pegu, who has repeatedly credited his mentor for shaping him both as a swimmer and as a person. “Sandeep sir feels like family now,” Pegu said. 
“He helped me not only in swimming but also in life. He taught me how elite athletes think and what it takes to compete at the highest level.”
Looking ahead, Pegu also wants to improve in the 50m butterfly and the 400m individual medley. “Improving in those races will help me become better in the 200m butterfly too,” he said.
With a Youth Olympic medal now around his neck, Pegu can finally savour a dream realised, one built on the sacrifices of his late father and the belief of those who helped him along the way.

briefs.headline: 'You always have the gun to your head': Ravi Shastri on life as India head coach
briefs.deck: Ravi Shastri expressed that coaching is more challenging than playing or commenting due to its immense responsibility. He mentioned the inability to control outcomes once players are on the field. Shastri reflected on the pressure to win consistently, regardless of conditions. He highlighted the satisfaction of achieving successful results and earning respect. His passion for cricket has kept him…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Former India head coach 
Ravi Shastri
 feels coaching is tougher than playing cricket or working as a commentator. He said the job comes with huge responsibility and pressure, as a coach has little control over what happens once the players step onto the field.
Known for his straight-talking nature and energetic commentary, Shastri shared his views on the three roles in an interview with Sky Sport's Ian Smith.
When asked which one he found the toughest, the former India coach picked coaching.
"Yeah, the toughest would be coaching, right. See, no, because you are nothing in your control once the players leave and get onto the field. You have the bat, ball when you're playing, the mic when you're broadcasting. But once the players go out, you know, you can only twiddle your thumbs. And it comes with immense responsibility. You know, the expectations of the country are such. COVID, no COVID, you got to win, you know, game after game. So there's no hiding behind that," Shastri said.
He also spoke about the pressure that comes with the job and the satisfaction of delivering results.
"You know, you always have the gun to your head. But if you pull it off and you're successful, I mean, then the rewards, it's very rewarding. 
Gives you tons of respect. And, you know, makes you enjoy what you're doing and gives you that kind of job satisfaction with nothing else gave you," he said.
Shastri was India's head coach from July 2017 to November 2021. His tenure saw the team achieve several major milestones, including two historic Test series victories in Australia.
India won their first-ever Test series in Australia during the 2018-19 Border-Gavaskar Trophy. They followed it up with another memorable 2-1 series win in 2020-21, despite several injury setbacks.
Under Shastri, India also held the No. 1 position in the ICC Test rankings for 42 months and reached the final of the inaugural World Test Championship in 2021. The team also made it to the semi-finals of the 2019 ODI World Cup.
‘The only way we can hang in here is if we are passionate’
Shastri also looked back at his journey in broadcasting and spoke about what has kept him connected to cricket for so many years.
He said his passion for the game has been the biggest reason behind his long association with the sport, despite having opportunities to explore other fields.
"[On his journey into broadcasting] it's amazing how life can take you in various places. And particularly the cricketing life. I mean it's captured us. I mean obviously you love the game. I mean you know to stay involved because you would have had many, many opportunities to break away and do other things with your stature in India. 
But you stayed with the game. And I love it. I mean the only way we can hang in here if we are passionate about the game," Shastri said.
"If you're not passionate about the game, you don't love the game, you won't be here this long with showing that kind of enthusiasm for every game day after day. You know, whether it's with you, the way you commentated on that World Cup final, you know, a close finish, you were calling it at the end. Fabulous. And we've called many finals in the end, you know, right through our careers. And it's a privilege, you know, when someone understands the game, understands the discipline of television, you know, and then to work that for that length of time. It's fun," he said.

briefs.headline: 'It's ridiculous': Ex-India coach questions Yashasvi Jaiswal's ODI snub
briefs.deck: Ryan ten Doeschate has voiced his bewilderment regarding Yashasvi Jaiswal's absence from India's ODI lineup. With an impressive record of two centuries in merely six matches, Jaiswal's exclusion raises questions, especially as the ODI World Cup looms. His notable performance against Mitchell Starc during the 2024 Test tour further strengthens his case. All eyes now turn to the forthcoming Test…
briefs.bodyText:
Former India assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate has questioned India's decision to keep 
Yashasvi Jaiswal
 out of the ODI team. He feels it is difficult to understand why a batter with so much talent and hunger to score runs is not getting a regular place in the side.
In six ODI matches, the left-hander has scored 285 runs, including two centuries, at an average of 71.25. However, despite these numbers, he has not been able to secure a regular place in India's white-ball teams.
With the 2027 ODI World Cup approaching, Jaiswal's chances of becoming a regular member of the first-choice team remain uncertain.
Speaking on the TalkSport Cricket Podcast, ten Doeschate spoke about Jaiswal's hunger to score runs and his disappointment when he misses out on big scores.
"He is so hungry to do well. You know, even when he gets runs but doesn't get a big one, the genuine disappointment in leaving runs out there, you can see it really hurts him. He is also, just touching on the ODI point, he is desperate to play ODI cricket as well. He doesn't get into the team, which is - it's crazy," said Doeschate.
‘It's ridiculous’: Ten Doeschate on Jaiswal's ODI omission
The former India assistant coach went a step further and described Jaiswal's absence from the ODI team as ridiculous. 
He also spoke about the young batter's hard work and dedication.
"It's ridiculous. There are some players we were chatting about yesterday who aren't in the team. But also just to be clear, you know, I wasn't the batting coach, so I didn't have that direct access to players in terms of working that closely with them. It was so I'd chip in here and there and maybe complement what the batting coach and the head coach were saying. But yeah, certainly very, very hungry, works very, very hard. One of those strange situations where he's actually not a great netter," he added.
Jaiswal's fearless approach against Starc
Ten Doeschate also recalled Jaiswal's performance during India's Test tour of Australia in 2024. He remembered how the youngster took on Mitchell Starc's pace and bounce in the first Test in Perth, despite struggling to deal with short balls during the practice sessions.
"I'll never forget, it happened in Australia, that whole build-up in Perth. And within the first three overs of the first Test match, Starc had bowled a 150k bouncer and he just pulled him in front of square. He just didn't look like he could play the short ball in the nets," he said.
Jaiswal in good form ahead of New Zealand Test series
Meanwhile, Jaiswal has been among the runs in the unofficial Test series against New Zealand A. The three-match series ended in a 0-0 draw after the fourth day's play in the third match was abandoned.
Jaiswal scored 17 and 5 in the first unofficial Test. He had a difficult start in the second match, getting out for a duck in the first innings. However, he bounced back with an unbeaten 155 in the second innings.
The left-hander continued his good form in the third unofficial Test, scoring another century with 102 runs.
Devdutt Padikkal, Jaiswal, Dhruv Jurel, Sai Sudharsan and Washington Sundar also got valuable time in the middle during the series. The first three batters scored four centuries between them.
The focus will now shift to the two-Test series between India and New Zealand. Both teams will look to secure a place in next year's World Test Championship final.
The first Test will begin on November 19 at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.

briefs.headline: Gurnoor Brar — the X-factor in India’s bowling cartel
briefs.deck: Gill has made no secret of his desire to have extra pace at his disposal to force the issue in the meandering middle overs. India can’t afford to be conservative in using Gurnoor in the lead-up to the mega event because he will only get better, more tactically astute and suave once he has more overs in his legs in the pressure-cooker situation of an international contest
briefs.bodyText:
Nothing sets the pulse racing more than watching a tearaway pace bowler in action. A long, never-ending run-up, an explosive build-up of momentum, the bowling crease attacked with ferocity, sometimes with a leap, culminates in the little orb being propelled at the rate of knots through a combination of shoulder and wrist and snappy fingers.
For long periods, India have yearned for a speed merchant, someone who can rattle opposition batting line-ups with naked, raw, untamed pace. It is said that Mohammad Nissar, who played in India’s first Test against England at Lord’s in June 1932, was frightfully pacy and deadly accurate. On India’s first day as a Test nation, he sent the stumps of openers Percy Holmes and Herbert Sutcliffe flying for six and three respectively, reducing the hosts to 11 for two.
Just 10 days previously, Holmes and Sutcliffe had put on a world record 555 for Yorkshire against Essex in the English County Championship. Nissar gave them a reality check and even though England recovered to post a 158-run victory, Nissar and his new-ball partner Amar Singh had given the home side a proper scare.

briefs.headline: WTA Chennai Open: Postponement of singles final sparks controversy
briefs.bodyText:
The postponement of the WTA 250 Chennai Open singles final due to rain and fireworks-induced smog on Sunday evening sparked controversy over the organisers’ handling of the situation.
The final, set for a 6:30 p.m. start, was delayed thrice due to rain. Once the rain relented for good, the organisers dried the centre court at the SDAT stadium and rescheduled the final at 9 p.m.
However, the smog caused by the Deepavali firecrackers had made the air quality hazardous and the match had to be shifted to 11 a.m. on Monday in which Poland’s Magda Linette defeated Indonesia’s Janice Tjen, the reigning champion, in three sets.
Christopher Bint, Tjen’s coach, in an Instagram story late on Sunday night, claimed that the organisers wanted to conduct the final despite the extremely poor air quality. “And they still wanted the match to go ahead,” he wrote, attaching a screenshot showing an AQI of 1556 in Chennai. Later, after Monday’s summit clash, Bint said, “Maybe, it could have just been postponed a little bit earlier.”
Linette felt the doubles final, which started at 4 p.m. on Sunday, could have been moved forward. “We should have put the doubles final way earlier which would have given us a lot of time,” said the 34-year-old Pole.
Hiten Joshi, the tournament director, said, “In these emergencies, the tournament supervisor (Sheetal Iyer) has to get permission from the WTA. So, they were going back and forth, and she also wanted to wait to see if any play was possible.”

briefs.headline: TPL to award scholarships to 36 junior players, two to get Australian Open opportunity
briefs.deck: The Race to Gold Masters will be held across three weekends in November, beginning with the North Zone event at the DLTA courts on November 14-15
briefs.bodyText:
The Tennis Premier League (TPL) will award scholarships worth ₹75,000 each to 36 promising junior players from six regions as part of its grassroots initiative, with two under-14 champions also earning an opportunity to travel to the 2027 Australian Open.
The Race to Gold Masters will be held across three weekends in November, beginning with the North Zone event at the DLTA courts on November 14-15.
The Gujarat Masters will follow on November 21-22 in Ahmedabad, before the Maharashtra leg in Mumbai on November 28-29.
The scholarships will cover tennis equipment, personalised apparel, professional guidance and opportunities to interact with leading Indian tennis players, including Leander Paes and Rohan Bopanna.
The programme is supported by Kia India, which has partnered with TPL for the first time.
